subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@novahealth.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@novahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap + next steps

Hi Lisa / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through NovaHealth's inference needs. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key pain points, goals, and an initial proposed plan so we have a shared reference. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

Summary of pain points
- Latency spikes during EHR ingestion and triage flows (95th p95 target currently 800–1200ms)
- Concern about data isolation & PHI handling for clinical models
- Predictable monthly spend required for budgeting — current variability from bursty workloads is a blocker for procurement

Goals / success criteria
1) Reserved/dedicated capacity (GPU pool) to guarantee baseline throughput for peak clinic hours
2) Network & tenancy isolation to satisfy security review (SOC2 + customer-managed KMS)
3) SLA targets: 99.9% uptime, p95 generation latency <= 450ms for standard request profile
4) Autoscaling burst capability to handle onboarding spikes without manual intervention

Initial recommended configuration (high-level)
- Dedicated capacity: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs in a private VPC (baseline), with a 2x burst pool for peak hours
- Model variant: quantized 8-bit of our recommended open model for clinical triage (we'll validate quality on your prompt set)
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for recent patient queries to reduce token compute during follow-ups

Next steps
1) I'll share a draft SOW that outlines the capacity, SLA, and expected ramp schedule (attached).
2) Monica (CS) will schedule a short eval run to validate latency/quality on your representative prompts next week.
3) Tom — could you confirm the expected steady-state RPS (requests per second) during clinic hours and a 2-week peak sample?
4) If these align, we can lock a month-to-month reserved plan for the first quarter while procurement completes PO.

Attachments: NovaHealth_Dedicated_Capacity_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Steady-state RPS: roughly 30–40 RPS during clinic hours (8am–6pm PST). Peak events (batch imports / post-update reprocessing) can touch 180–220 RPS for short windows (10–45 minutes).
2) Latency: our internal goal for the triage path is p95 <= 400ms; we can be flexible to 450ms as long as we have consistent monitoring & alerting.
3) Data handling: we need the option for customer-managed KMS and audit log access for the last 12 months.

Assuming the 8x baseline configuration you proposed, can Redwood commit to an autoscaling policy that adds burst capacity within 90 seconds of sustained elevated RPS? Also — procurement asked for an outline of escalation paths and credits for SLA misses; can you include that in the SOW?

I'll review the attached SOW and circle back with Lisa and procurement by end of day Thursday.

Thanks,
Tom
Sr. Platform Engineer, NovaHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@novahealth.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@novahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap + next steps

Tom — thanks for the quick clarifications, this lines up well. A few action items and confirmations from our side: 

- Autoscaling: we can commit to a policy that brings burst capacity online within ~60–120s for sustained RPS increases. We'll include the specific trigger thresholds in the SOW (e.g., sustained 75% baseline utilization for >60s).
- SLA & credits: added a section in the SOW draft that outlines uptime targets (99.9%) and a credits table (pro-rated) for SLO misses. We'll also include a named escalation path with 24x7 on-call contacts and SLA response windows.
- KMS & audit logs: private deployment option supports customer-managed KMS; we can expose audit logs for 12 months and provide a snapshot export for procurement review.

I attached an updated SOW draft (NovaHealth_Dedicated_Capacity_SOW_v1.pdf) that includes the autoscale triggers, SLA credits table, and preliminary pricing for the 8+2 configuration. Pricing notes are intentionally high level; once we validate latency and usage on your prompt set, we can lock committed usage pricing.

Proposed ramp / pilot timeline
- Week 1: Eval run — Monica will run a 48-hour latency/quality validation on a representative prompt set (Monica will reach out to schedule).
- Week 2–3: Pilot on dedicated 4x baseline + 1x burst to validate autoscaling behavior with your production traffic pattern.
- End of Week 4: If pilot metrics meet p95 and throughput targets, cutover to 8x baseline reserved capacity and finalize procurement terms.

Next steps for you
- Tom: confirm the 2-week peak sample and share any existing traffic logs (redacted) for Monica to run the eval.
- Lisa: procurement will need the SOW + escalation contact and a simple PO template — I can send those as separate attachments if helpful.

I pasted the SOW link and a HubSpot record below for reference. Happy to hop on a quick 15-minute call if you want to walk the SOW.

Related links:

Best,
